examples.label: Current user and privileges (the key check)
Group memberships - look for privileged groups

notes:
=== USER AND GROUP ENUMERATION ===
Group membership surfaces indirect privilege paths that don't appear in whoami /priv.

COMMANDS:
net user <username>                          → full user details including group membership
net localgroup                               → all local groups
net localgroup "Backup Operators"            → list members of specific group
Get-LocalGroupMember -Group "Administrators" → PowerShell equivalent
Get-ADPrincipalGroupMembership $env:USERNAME → domain group membership

HIGH-VALUE GROUPS TO CHECK (in priority order):
1. Administrators / Domain Admins → already privileged
2. Backup Operators → SeBackupPrivilege → NTDS.dit → domain compromise
3. Server Operators → SERVICE_ALL_ACCESS on DC services → SYSTEM on DC
4. Print Operators → SeLoadDriverPrivilege → kernel driver exploit
5. DnsAdmins → ServerLevelPluginDll → SYSTEM via DNS service on DC
6. Hyper-V Administrators → clone DC VM → offline NTDS.dit extraction
7. Event Log Readers → read Security log → credential harvest from 4688 events
8. Account Operators → modify user/group accounts → group manipulation
9. Schema Admins → modify AD schema → backdoor default object ACLs

=== WINDOWS PRIVILEGES QUICK REFERENCE ===
SeImpersonatePrivilege → JuicyPotato / PrintSpoofer / RoguePotato
SeDebugPrivilege       → LSASS dump (ProcDump) + psgetsystem (SYSTEM via parent process)
SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege → takeown any file → icacls grant → read SAM/NTDS/web.config
SeBackupPrivilege      → FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS → bypass ACL on any file
SeLoadDriverPrivilege  → load Capcom.sys → kernel-level SYSTEM execution
SeRestorePrivilege     → write anywhere on filesystem

EVENT ID 4672 fires on any logon with sensitive privileges in token.
Baseline expected accounts, alert on deviations.

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
Standard user + Backup Operators membership = path to all domain hashes (NTDS.dit)
Service account + SeImpersonate = reliable SYSTEM (Potato attacks)
Developer account + SeDebugPrivilege = LSASS dump + psgetsystem

recommended.note: SeTakeOwnership -> seize and read any file.

name: WinPE - User, Group and Privilege Enumeration
description: Enumerates the current token's privileges and group memberships plus local users/groups. whoami /priv is the key check - SeImpersonate, SeDebug, SeBackup, SeTakeOwnership, SeLoadDriver each map to a specific escalation path.

variations.label: Local users/groups
variations.command:
net user
net localgroup
net localgroup administrators
net accounts
query user

variations.label: PS local groups
variations.command:
Get-LocalGroup | Select-Object Name,Description
Get-LocalGroupMember Administrators
Get-LocalGroupMember '<group>'

variations.label: Installed software (registry)
variations.command:
Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*' | Select DisplayName,DisplayVersion
Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*' | Select DisplayName,DisplayVersion
